hyperedges.name: Four Pillars of Waku
hyperedges.description: The four foundational architectural pillars that together make up Waku

hyperedges.name: Graph Workflow Nodes
hyperedges.description: All components involved in graph workflow execution

hyperedges.name: Benchmark Evaluation Axes
hyperedges.description: The four dimensions used to score models in the benchmark

hyperedges.label: pi Extensibility Architecture
hyperedges.description: Four complementary mechanisms enabling pi's extensibility from 0 tokens (skills) to shipping (packages), each solving the context-overhead problem differently

hyperedges.label: Memory Backend Comparison
hyperedges.description: Four memory products tested on identical five-beat protocol to expose their different retention and contradiction-resolution strategies

hyperedges.label: Multi-Agent Memory Synchronization
hyperedges.description: Waku Memory as the shared backbone enabling consistent memory access across independent agents (Grok, Muse, Claude Code, Codex, Waku)

hyperedges.label: Four-pillar agent architecture
hyperedges.description: Complete system design for Waku agent: Harness handles execution, Loop executes decisions, Memory stores knowledge, Eval/LLM-Ops observes and judges

hyperedges.label: Skill capabilities shared across agents
hyperedges.description: Exportable skills that extend agent functionality and can be deployed to multiple agents via skill export mechanism

hyperedges.label: Cross-agent memory and harness integration
hyperedges.description: Three complementary views of how personal agents (Grok Bot, Muse, Waku) share memory and job execution through Waku Memory hosted service

hyperedges.label: LLM Provider Ecosystem
hyperedges.description: Collection of multiple LLM provider logos enabling provider switching and multi-model support in Waku

hyperedges.label: Messaging Platform Integrations
hyperedges.description: Collection of messaging platform logos representing multi-channel communication access points to Waku

hyperedges.label: Memory System Backends
hyperedges.description: Collection of memory system logos providing pluggable backends for persistent context management

hyperedges.label: LLM Provider Integration Logos
hyperedges.description: Unified collection of provider logos used in Waku UI for displaying available LLM services and integrations

nodes.label: Mixture of Experts (MoE)
nodes.description: Architecture with many small expert sub-networks (896) plus a router that picks relevant experts (16) per word, only evaluating selected experts

nodes.label: KDA (Kimi Delta Attention)
nodes.description: Linear attention mechanism computing running-average instead of re-summing everything each step, using delta rule updates

nodes.label: AttnRes (Attention Residuals)
nodes.description: Mechanism allowing layers to reuse any earlier layer's work, not just the previous one, via learned weighted combination

nodes.label: K3 Price Tag Rationale

nodes.label: Harness - local-first agent execution
nodes.description: The foundation pillar that runs agents locally, via Docker, SSH, or VPS. Never sends secrets or keys. Carries memory, calendar, chat history
nodes.rationale: Local-first design ensures user privacy and data sovereignty while enabling persistent agent execution

nodes.label: Loop - agent decision-making cycle
nodes.description: The core agentic loop with five decision points: model choice, memory retrieval, tool selection, safety gate, and result verification
nodes.rationale: Structured loop enables deterministic evaluation and clear failure modes

nodes.label: Memory - three-tier knowledge storage
nodes.description: Procedural memory (skills, instructions), Semantic memory (facts, user profile), Episode memory (chat history, past events)
nodes.rationale: Layered memory architecture balances recency with long-term patterns

nodes.label: Eval/LLM-Ops - observability and judgment
nodes.description: Observes agent behavior through tracing and judges outputs with LLM-as-judge. Arena races models. Release gate blocks deployments on eval failures
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and judge-based evaluation enables safe iteration and reproducible testing

nodes.label: Four pillars of Waku agent architecture
nodes.description: Harness (local execution), Loop (decision cycle), Memory (knowledge storage), Eval/LLM-Ops (observability and judgment)
nodes.norm_label: four pillars of waku agent architecture
